question: A matrix $A$ has $2$ rows and $8$ elements. Its entries, read row-wise, are $1,2,0,-1,3,1,2,0$. Determine the order of $A$, write it in matrix form, and then calculate $AB$ for $$B=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&2\\2&1&-1\\0&3&1\\1&2&0\end{bmatrix},$$ justifying that the multiplication is defined and stating the order of the resulting matrix.
explanation:
Determination of Order

If $A$ has $2$ rows and $n$ columns, then the number of elements is $2n$. Since $A$ contains $8$ elements, $2n=8$, giving $n=4$. Therefore, the order of $A$ is $2\times4$. Reading the given entries row-wise, $$A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&0&-1\\3&1&2&0\end{bmatrix}$$ The matrix $B$ has order $4\times3$. Since the number of columns of $A$ is $4$, which equals the number of rows of $B$, the product $AB$ is defined and will have order $2\times3$.

Evaluation

Now, $$AB=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&0&-1\\3&1&2&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&0&2\\2&1&-1\\0&3&1\\1&2&0\end{bmatrix}$$ The entries of the first row are $1(1)+2(2)+0(0)-1(1)=4$, $1(0)+2(1)+0(3)-1(2)=0$ and $1(2)+2(-1)+0(1)-1(0)=0$. The entries of the second row are $3(1)+1(2)+2(0)+0(1)=5$, $3(0)+1(1)+2(3)+0(2)=7$ and $3(2)+1(-1)+2(1)+0(0)=7$. Hence, $$AB=\begin{bmatrix}4&0&0\\5&7&7\end{bmatrix}$$ Therefore, $A$ is of order $2\times4$, the multiplication $AB$ is defined, and the product is a matrix of order $2\times3$.
